name: Pharmaceutical Product Launch Strategy
description: An evidence-led pharmaceutical commercialization system with a confidential navy cover, disciplined light analysis pages, gold milestones, teal differentiation, and explicit compliance guardrails.
style_guide:
# Pharmaceutical Product Launch Strategy

## Visual concept

This English-language style is designed for pharmaceutical product managers, commercialization teams, medical affairs, market access, and launch governance. It combines a confidential deep-navy cover with warm-white evidence pages, producing a deck that feels rigorous, executive, and launch-ready rather than promotional. Gold identifies strategic priorities and milestones, teal marks differentiation or access, and orange-red is reserved for material compliance risk. Every page should connect evidence to one commercial decision while keeping scientific, regulatory, access, and patient-support boundaries explicit.

## Canvas, grid, and safe area

- Use a fixed `1280 x 720 px` canvas in a 16:9 ratio.
- Keep `54–68 px` safe margins. The cover image may bleed to all edges, while titles, claims, confidential markings, and metadata stay inside the safe area.
- Use a 12-column grid with `18–22 px` gutters. Typical layouts are 5/7 cover thesis-plus-metadata, 5/7 KPI-plus-patient-journey, 7/5 value-table-plus-pillars, and 6/6 market-funnel-plus-competition.
- Reserve a narrow navy rule across the top of analytical pages. Place a gold section label beneath it and a quiet deck identifier, source, or page count along the bottom.
- Keep the main conclusion headline in the upper quarter, followed immediately by one evidence-framing sentence.
- Align tables, cards, chart frames, patient-journey nodes, risk columns, and timeline gates to shared guides.
- Use `18–24 px` between modules. Dense evidence is acceptable only when hierarchy, labels, and reading order remain unambiguous.

## Color system

### Core colors

- Launch navy: `#0B213E`. Use for the cover, top rules, positioning panels, selected cards, table headers, and primary chart series.
- Midnight black: `#071426`. Use for deep cover shadows, confidential fields, and maximum-contrast type areas.
- Evidence paper: `#F4F0E8`. Use as the primary analytical-page background.
- Clinical white: `#FFFFFF`. Use for cards, charts, tables, and high-contrast type on navy.
- Milestone gold: `#D9A744`. Use for priorities, target states, product columns, phase gates, and strategic emphasis.

### Supporting colors

- Differentiation teal: `#2F8A88`. Use for clinical differentiation, access, secondary series, and expansion segments.
- Risk orange: `#C95832`. Use only for high-severity compliance or operational risk.
- Slate text: `#5C6878`. Use for body copy, methodology, captions, and source notes.
- Grid stone: `#D9D6CF`. Use for dividers, inactive bars, chart grids, and timeline rails.

### Usage rules

- Launch navy and Evidence paper define the system. The cover is dark; analytical pages are light so detailed evidence remains inspectable.
- Gold is the primary strategic accent. Teal identifies a distinct value, segment, or access dimension; do not swap their meanings page to page.
- Use Risk orange only with a written severity and named mitigation. Do not use it as decorative emphasis.
- Limit analytical pages to navy, gold, teal, and one risk color. Direct-label all series and status categories.
- Do not use gradients in charts or text. A subtle dark photographic overlay is permitted only on the cover.

## Typography

- Primary font: `Inter`, `Aptos`, or `Arial`; fallback: `Helvetica Neue, system-ui, sans-serif`.
- Use a strong sans serif with bold weights for commercial conclusions and a true italic for one highlighted phrase.
- Cover title: `56–76 px`, weight `750–900`, line-height `0.98–1.06`; use Milestone gold italic for the launch phrase.
- Analytical headline: `40–52 px`, weight `750–900`, line-height `1.02–1.1`; use Differentiation teal italic for one strategic qualifier.
- Section label: `10–13 px`, weight `700`, uppercase with `3–5 px` tracking, Milestone gold.
- Hero metric: `42–62 px`, weight `700–850`; keep units smaller and baseline context nearby.
- Panel title: `19–26 px`, weight `700–800`.
- Body copy: `13–17 px`, weight `400–500`, line-height `1.35–1.55`.
- Table text and chart labels: `11–15 px`; source, methodology, and confidential notes: `9–11 px`.
- Use tabular numerals for clinical endpoints, market sizes, costs, shares, dates, and targets.
- Do not shrink references or safety context below readable size to make room for another claim.

## Layout and components

- Analytical cards use Clinical white, square corners, a `1 px` Grid stone border, and no drop shadow. One selected card may invert to Launch navy or fill with Milestone gold.
- Disease-landscape KPI blocks show one value, unit, definition, population, time frame, and source. Arrange them in a disciplined 2x2 grid.
- Patient journeys use five or fewer numbered nodes linked by a thin gold line. The final gap or opportunity node may use Milestone gold.
- Positioning statements use a full-width Launch navy panel with white copy and one gold product or value phrase.
- Clinical value tables use a dark header, one highlighted product column, aligned endpoint rows, and direct study context above.
- Commercial-pillar cards use a colored left rail, a large two-digit index, one decision statement, and a short evidence line.
- HCP prioritization uses a proportional three-tier funnel with target count, role, reach strategy, and prescription contribution beside each tier.
- Channel cards use a `4 px` top rail, a numbered channel title, four activities, and budget share anchored at the bottom.
- Compliance tables use explicit severity, mitigation, and owner columns. KPI rows use one left rail and one right-aligned target.

## Charts and data

- Favor patient pathways, KPI cards, clinical value tables, HCP funnels, competitive bars, channel allocation cards, risk tables, and regulatory-gated timelines.
- Launch navy is the primary series, Teal is the secondary series, Gold indicates the proposed product or target, and Risk orange marks only material exposure.
- Every scientific or commercial value needs a source, population, period, unit, and status such as observed, forecast, target, or illustrative.
- Keep clinical endpoints comparable. State study design, analysis set, time point, comparator, and whether comparisons are direct or indirect.
- Market sizing should distinguish diagnosed, treated, eligible, accessible, and targeted populations. Do not collapse them into one opportunity number.
- Funnel and channel data require a common denominator and reporting window. Budget shares should reconcile to 100 percent.
- Regulatory, medical, legal, privacy, pharmacovigilance, and promotional-review gates must be shown as dependencies, not footnotes.
- Do not reuse preview product names, trial data, claims, competitor results, market shares, or approval milestones. All visible evidence must be verified for the actual asset and jurisdiction.

## Page variations

- Cover: full-bleed dark pharmaceutical photography, a left-aligned white and gold title, confidential marker, short commercialization subtitle, and a disciplined presenter/company/date block.
- Disease area and unmet need: four KPI cards on the left, a patient-journey panel on the right, and one strategic insight rail beneath it.
- Product positioning and clinical value: a full-width positioning panel, a large evidence table, and three stacked commercial-pillar cards.
- Target physicians, patients, and market structure: HCP prioritization funnel and patient-segment cards on the left, competitive share bars and a play-space conclusion on the right.
- Launch channels, education, and promotion: four equal channel cards across the body and one phased sequencing bar from pre-launch through sustain.
- KPIs, compliance, and timeline: KPI rows on the left, a risk-and-owner table on the right, and a regulatory-gated critical path across the bottom.

## Imagery and icons

- Use relevant laboratory, packaging, delivery-device, molecule, specialist-care, or patient-pathway imagery only when it supports the launch context.
- The cover may use a dark, highly controlled product or laboratory crop with enough negative space for the title.
- Analytical pages should prioritize tables, diagrams, and charts over stock photography.
- Avoid identifiable patients, unapproved pack shots, unsupported mechanism imagery, or visual claims that exceed the approved evidence.
- Icons should be rare, simple, and single-color. Use them only to clarify channels, gates, or roles.

## Avoid

- Do not make the deck resemble consumer advertising, a science-fiction technology pitch, or a generic blue consulting template.
- Do not copy preview company, asset, trial, endpoint, competitor, market, timeline, channel, or KPI data.
- Do not use unsupported efficacy, safety, adherence, access, superiority, or patient-preference claims.
- Do not use gradients in data, glossy 3D molecules, decorative DNA imagery, oversized pills, or dense icon grids.
- Do not mix medical education and promotion without the required review and jurisdictional boundary.
- Do not hide safety, privacy, pharmacovigilance, fair-market-value, off-label, or adverse-event obligations in tiny text.
- Do not present forecasts as actuals, targets as commitments, indirect comparisons as head-to-head evidence, or regulatory dates as guaranteed.
